description: Equipo interdisciplinario de estudiantes de Ingeniería en Sistemas e Ingeniería Industrial, enfocado en el desarrollo de soluciones basadas en datos, tecnología y optimización.
summary:
Citax+ turns two generations of NASA fire satellites into one consistent fire history for Argentina, and adds a 30-day fire-risk outlook. MODIS has observed active fires since 2000, but VIIRS (since 2012) detects about 5× more, smaller fires, so naively joining both records creates a false jump in 2012. We built a neural network that translates MODIS hotspot counts into VIIRS-equivalent counts. Using NASA FIRMS data, we aggregated detections into a 0.25° grid by month and day/night pass and trained on the years Aqua and S-NPP flew together (2012 to mid-2021). Tested on unseen years against NOAA-20, the model reproduces VIIRS within 13.6% at 2° zones and 3.9% for the whole country, close to the 9.3% that two VIIRS satellites differ from each other. The result is a continuous monthly record from 2000 to 2025. In a web app, firefighters, farmers and planners pick an area by name, location or drawing, see which months historically burn the most, spot anomalous months, check today's detections with satellite imagery, and download the data.

By consolidating both satellite records into a consistent historical dataset, Citax+ provides more reliable historical statistics, creating a stronger foundation for identifying patterns and making more accurate future fire-risk predictions.
details:
What it does

Citax+ builds a single, comparable fire history for Argentina from 2000 to 2025 by harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detections, and presents it in a web app built around a full-screen map:

- 30-day fire risk (default view): probability of at least one fire in each 27 km cell over the next 30 days, compared with what is usual for those dates.

- Place panel: tap a cell to see how that place burns through a typical year (monthly curve, worst year) and its 30-day risk.

- Burning calendar for any area and period: a year × month grid colored by fire count or by anomaly against the historical median, with the critical season, anomalous years, trend, and most active months and years. For example, February 2022 in the Esteros del Iberá area had 12,994 hotspots versus a median of 450 for that month, about 29× the usual and the highest in 25 years.

- Near-real-time detections from FIRMS for a day or a range of up to 10 days, with Sentinel-2 before/after imagery for each fire.

- Choosing an area: search by city or province, use your location, type coordinates, or draw a rectangle on the map.

- Downloads: detections, calendar and monthly series as CSV tables, and the calendar as an image.

- Accessibility: plain-language explanations for every figure, four color palettes for different kinds of color blindness, and a phone layout.

How it works

1. Data: NASA FIRMS standard-processing active-fire archives for Argentina (MODIS Collection 6.1 on Terra and Aqua; VIIRS 375 m on S-NPP and NOAA-20), and the FIRMS API for near-real-time detections.

2. Cleaning: vegetation fires only (type 0), low-confidence detections excluded, exact duplicates removed.

3. Grid: detections counted on a 0.25° grid, by month and by day/night overpass. Days when a satellite had no valid pass are detected and excluded, so data gaps are not confused with "no fire".

4. Sensor pairing: Aqua (MODIS) and S-NPP (VIIRS) cross the equator at nearly the same time, so their overlap from January 2012 to June 2021 is used for training. Aqua's orbit drifts after mid-2021, so later years use VIIRS directly.

5. Model: a Poisson neural network that predicts VIIRS = Aqua count × a learned ratio + extra fires MODIS cannot see (MLP 3×64, ensemble of 3). We started from a team member's first version and improved it with 48 inputs: Terra detections, low-confidence and scan-edge Aqua detections, overpass time, neighboring cells, the next month, the cell's typical month, and conversion rates per zone and per cell learned only from training years. The improved model cut the error from 18.0% to 13.6% at 2° zones and from 7.0% to 3.9% at country level, and fixed the underestimate in the largest fires.

6. Validation: train up to 2017, validate 2018–2019, test 2020 to mid-2021 against NOAA-20; plus a backward test (train on recent years, test 2012–2014, 15.4% error at 2° zones) to check that the translation holds for the years before VIIRS. The S-NPP vs NOAA-20 disagreement (9.3%) is the practical floor any model can reach.

7. Output: a monthly VIIRS-equivalent series per grid cell from November 2000 to December 2025: VIIRS observed since 2012, MODIS Aqua translated by the network from July 2002, and Terra-only months (2000–2002) bridged with a simpler per-zone ratio. Each estimate carries an 80% range from its out-of-sample errors.

8. Serving: the series is precomputed and served by a FastAPI service; a Cloudflare Worker serves FIRMS, the 30-day risk forecast (recent detections plus each cell's seasonal history) and Sentinel-2 imagery from Google Earth Engine; the web app is React + Leaflet.

Benefits and impact

- Removes the artificial 2012 jump, so 25 years of fire activity can be compared fairly.

- Shows when each area historically burns the most, to plan firebreaks, brigades and water before the season.

- Flags anomalous months for early warnings and post-season analysis, and gives a 30-day risk outlook.

- Open, downloadable data for researchers and local agencies.

Citax+ estimates probabilities and describes historical patterns; it does not predict the exact date or place of a fire.

Tools

Python, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, DuckDB, PyTorch, FastAPI; TypeScript, React, Vite, Leaflet, three.js and anime.js for the web app; Cloudflare Workers and Containers for hosting; Google Earth Engine for Sentinel-2 imagery; HTML/JavaScript with GSAP and HyperFrames for the animated demo; MediaPipe to trace the team's cartoon characters from our own photos.

Creativity and factors considered

We focused on fair comparison: matching overpass times, explicit exposure (valid pass days), gap detection at the pass level, honest error reporting by zone size with an 80% range for every estimate, and medians instead of means for "typical month" baselines, because fire counts are highly skewed. Every figure in the app has a plain-language explanation, and the color scales work for people with color blindness. The demo is a short animated story of a farmer told by the team as cartoon characters.
